items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: We was playing Erico's Creole Band, started gigging with him.

ctx.x: were doing acts of and they couldn't arrest them. And they were getting angrier and angrier. 'You can't touch me.' And they'd slap the women. 'You can't touch me.'

So they were angry, too. So all right, I see all this happening. So I started gigging around with a few friends, you know, that I knew. We was playing Erico's Creole Band, started gigging with him. And I went to the old place I used to work, it's called the Chez Florence, where Louis used to be. And this woman recognizes me and says, I want you to make a band. And I was hurting, too. And she had an apartment there, she had a apartment.

Now, I didn't know that -- I was playing downstairs and I could see how those people would go back in there and everything, upstairs, there'd be parties up there, and they'd be doing business. Those kings and things would disappear and they'd be up there having their smoke.
